title: Remove live authored parts from individual-part generation correspondence
description:
## Summary
Implement outside-handoff A2 so individual-part compiled generation data carries resolved part snapshots instead of live `CreaturePart` references.

## User Mandate
> Continue

STRICT. Binding constraints: continue the outside-audit-ordered implementation wave; preserve `CreatureDefinition` as authoring authority; keep generated correspondence detached from later authored mutation; retain raw-definition overloads only as outer compatibility boundaries; record focused validation evidence.

## Scope
- Add one concrete `ResolvedPartProgram` value containing `ResolvedPartSnapshot` and `SdfProgram`.
- Make `CompileIndividualPartsPortable` return the concrete correspondence in stable ID order.
- Migrate appearance and generation consumers and disposal paths.
- Add snapshot mutation regression coverage.
- Do not add generic result hierarchies, service locators, or a second snapshot architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No live `CreaturePart` reference survives in individual-part generation results.
- Stable part identity and appearance data remain available from the resolved correspondence.
- Mutating authored DNA after correspondence creation does not change generated correspondence data.
- Managed and Burst appearance paths continue to compile and produce existing output.
- Focused build, Unity runtime tests, console inspection, and diff validation pass.

## Validation
Pending task closure evidence.

## Findings
The handoff identifies A2 as the next slice after A1. The prior compiler returned tuples containing `CreaturePart`, obtained through `definition.FindPart`, which crossed the snapshot boundary.

## Blockers
A first Unity test attempt may require retry if the editor test job does not initialize; this is an environment risk, not a code acceptance criterion.

## Next Step
Record implementation and validation evidence, then proceed to the next handoff dependency-ready slice.

comments.body:
## Implementation Evidence
- Added concrete `ResolvedPartProgram` in `SdfProgram.cs`, containing detached `ResolvedPartSnapshot` data and the owned `SdfProgram`.
- Changed `SdfProgramBuilder.CompileIndividualPartsPortable` to return stable ID-ordered `List<ResolvedPartProgram>` and removed the `definition.FindPart` lookup from the generated correspondence.
- Migrated `AppearanceBaker`, `AppearanceResolveBurst`, `PartAppearanceSampler`, and `CreatureMeshGenerator` to consume the resolved correspondence and preserve program disposal ownership.
- Added `CompileIndividualPartsPortable_CapturesResolvedAppearanceAfterAuthoredMutation` to prove authored appearance mutation does not alter generated correspondence data.

## Validation Evidence
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore`: passed, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Unity 6000.5.9f1 PlayMode assembly `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime`: 465/465 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Unity console after the successful run: no product errors or warnings; only test-result save and post-build cleanup logs.
- Editor diagnostics: no errors in all seven changed source/test files.
- `git diff --check`: passed; only existing line-ending normalization warnings were reported.
- The first Unity attempt timed out before test discovery; the immediate retry succeeded and is the authoritative runtime result.

## Findings
The A2 boundary is now concrete: generated individual-part data retains stable identity and resolved appearance without retaining an authored `CreaturePart` reference. Raw-definition overloads still resolve a snapshot at the outer compatibility boundary.

## Residual Risk
The appearance files already contained unrelated pre-existing worktree changes, so their combined diff should be reviewed carefully before commit. No new managed copy, generic result hierarchy, or alternative snapshot path was introduced.

## Next Step
Proceed to the next audit dependency-ready slice, likely A3 primitive SDF emission consolidation or B1 canonical snapshot/revision authority.
